correctness.rationale: The first-step system is exact for all non-source vertices on each shore. The positive denominator gives unique potentials. On a fixed sub-shore budget, the support difference identifies the bottleneck, and the closed identity B-u(d) reduces budget optimization to a rational one-variable function. Its derivative numerator is strictly decreasing, hence the score has no interior maximum. This leaves exactly the balanced or one-shore endpoint profiles. Explicit score subtraction gives a strictly decreasing quadratic with a unique critical fidelity. The n<=k boundary uses h_v<=lambda for every non-source and strictness when both shores retain a non-source. All boundaries k=1, k=n, k=2n and 0<lambda<1 are handled. Exact graph-level rational linear-system replay agrees for 8136 subsets through n=5 and verifies the eight-set example.

originality.rationale: The initiating September 2026 work defines the invariant and provides general distance, submodularity and optimization theorems, with the accessible special-family descriptions centered on complete graphs, stars and spiders. The present result supplies a distinct explicit optimal-budget phase diagram for balanced bicliques, all maximizing source profiles, an irrational parity-dependent changeover and exact optimizer counts. Earlier group hitting probability work studies fixed-start evaluation/ranking, which cannot imply a uniform-in-start maximin budget classification. Targeted database and web searches under source-placement, first-hitting, maximin, group-hitting, K_{n,n} and phase transition formulations returned no covering theorem. The later parts of the initiating source were not fully retrievable, so an unadvertised related lemma remains a stated risk, not treated as proof of absence.
residual_risks: Later sections and possible appendices of arXiv:2609.31535v1 were not retrievable through the accessible public interfaces despite bounded alternatives; an unstated related lemma could overlap.
The algebraic budget optimizer could have been obtained previously under penalized/group hitting probability or killed-walk fairness terminology not surfaced by the searches.

A general graph optimization formulation can numerically recover any given small instance; the originality claim is for the exact all-parameter phase theorem and complete optimizer classification, not basic computability.

value.rationale: For a newly studied uniform discounted hitting-domination invariant, the theorem solves the complete finite-budget problem on the canonical balanced bipartite test family, including all optimum sets and their counts. The budget/discount interaction exhibits a genuinely nontrivial parity-dependent switch at an irrational algebraic threshold between spreading source placements and putting all sources on one shore. On K_{4,4}, rational lambda and tau produce exactly eight one-shore minimum solutions, so the structural transition directly changes the optimal design. The result also replaces general mixed-integer optimization by explicit constant-time score evaluations for each budget and an exact minimum threshold rule; it is not merely a finite computation or a restatement of distance domination.
